name: Pennsylvania

notes: Food for home consumption is exempt, candy and gum included, but soft drinks are taxed at the full rate, which is not counted here.

Alcohol bought in stores: bottles and cans bought in stores pay the sales tax. Spirits and wine from the state's stores also carry the 18% liquor tax in their price, which isn't counted here: it doesn't fall on beer, and no official figure gives the share of spirits and wine (liquor stores' national share of alcohol bought in stores, used for Mississippi's taxes on package stores, doesn't fit: it counts beer distributors too, and this tax falls on spirits and wine, including wine sold in grocery stores, not on a kind of store). Beer bought from distributors pays the sales tax, and so do state stores' sales, with Philadelphia's 2% and Allegheny County's 1% on top; six-packs bought at bars and licensed grocery stores pay none at the sale (the licensee paid it when buying), which isn't taken out here.
Drinks served at bars and restaurants are not subject to the sales tax; Philadelphia's 10% liquor tax and Allegheny County's 7% drink tax apply to them instead, counted there (local rates table).
Cigarettes, other tobacco and e-cigarettes are taxed at the general rate, on top of their excise taxes.
Household supplies: toilet tissue, disposable diapers and incontinence products are exempt, which is not taken out here; napkins, paper towels and detergents are taxed.
Personal care products: toothpaste, toothbrushes, dental floss and menstrual products are exempt, which is not taken out here; soap, shampoo, deodorant and cosmetics are taxed.
Barber and beauty services, and laundry and dry cleaning: not taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Clothing: most clothing and footwear are exempt. Jewelry and watches (accessories under 61 Pa. Code 53.1, which names jewelry) are taxed at 6% and counted on their share of US sales of clothing, shoes and jewelry (13%, 2022 Economic Census), 0.78% of what is spent on clothing, shoes and jewelry; the category's rate also takes in laundry and dry cleaning, at their own rate. Other accessories, formal wear, furs and sports clothing are taxed too but not counted, since no official figure gives their share, nor is Philadelphia's or Allegheny County's local tax on jewelry.

Motor fuel is exempt from sales tax; the oil company franchise tax, left out here, is 57.6 cents a gallon for 2026 (unchanged from 2025) plus a 1.1-cent underground storage tank fee; 2026 bills for a gas tax holiday were not enacted (reported).
Auto repair labor: taxed (FTA 2017 survey answer).

Act 21 of 2026 (enacted July 12, 2026) has sellers that collect the state tax also collect Philadelphia's 2% and Allegheny County's 1% on sales delivered there, wherever the seller is (destination sourcing), for tax periods from January 1, 2026, enforced from October 1, 2026; it changes no rate (Department of Revenue).

Hotel stays pay the 6% state hotel occupancy tax instead of sales tax (7% in Allegheny County and Philadelphia), plus local hotel taxes such as Philadelphia's 8.5% and Allegheny County's 7% (reported), which are not counted here (Department of Revenue; City of Philadelphia).
gaps: Pennsylvania local sales tax exists only in Allegheny County (1%, countywide, Pittsburgh included) and Philadelphia (2%); every place takes its county rate, so "places" is empty.

Drinks served at bars and restaurants pay no sales tax, state or local; Philadelphia's 10% liquor tax and Allegheny County's 7% drink tax fall on them instead and are counted in those counties' alcohol rates for drinks served (City of Philadelphia, liquor tax; Allegheny County Code, Alcoholic Beverage Tax).
Clothing and groceries are exempt in Pennsylvania, which their categories use; the rate here is the general one.

42101: Philadelphia taxes sweetened drinks, including diet drinks, at 1.5 cents an ounce (the Philadelphia Beverage Tax, since January 2017; the city, phila.gov). It is an excise tax on distributors, not a sales tax, so it is not in the sales-tax figures here.
